title: Probing Chemical Language Models: Effects of Pre-training and Fine-tuning
abstract: arXiv:2607.02140v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Chemical language models (CLMs) are trained with linearized representations such as SMILES, yet it remains unclear which chemically meaningful substructures they encode. To foster a better understanding of CLMs, we conduct a systematic study and probe for 78 molecular substructures across eight pre-trained and six randomly initialized models. We furthermore study how fine-tuning on chemical downstream tasks affects the learned representations of molecular substructures. Our results show that pre-training generally improves molecular structure awareness of CLMs, particularly in the upper layers. Moreover, randomly initialized models already encode ring structures well in the first layer. Our analysis on two chemical downstream tasks further reveals that, interestingly, fine-tuning affects task-relevant molecular substructures more than others, indicating that the changes in the representations follow chemical theory.

translated_title: 探测化学语言模型：预训练与微调的影响
translated_abstract: 化学语言模型（CLMs）使用诸如SMILES之类的线性化表示进行训练，然而它们编码了哪些具有化学意义的子结构仍不清楚。为了促进对CLMs的更好理解，我们进行了一项系统性研究，在八个预训练模型和六个随机初始化模型中探测了78种分子子结构。我们进一步研究了在化学下游任务上进行微调如何影响所学习到的分子子结构表示。我们的结果表明，预训练普遍提升了CLMs对分子结构的感知能力，尤其是在模型的上层。此外，随机初始化的模型在第一层就已经能很好地编码环状结构。我们对两个化学下游任务的分析进一步揭示了一个有趣的现象：微调对与任务相关的分子子结构的影响大于其他子结构，这表明表示的变化遵循化学理论。
tldr: 该研究通过系统探测78种分子子结构，揭示了预训练能提升化学语言模型的分子结构感知能力（尤以上层显著），且微调主要改变与任务相关的子结构表示，表明模型的表示变化遵循化学理论。
en_tdlr: This study systematically probes 78 molecular substructures in chemical language models, revealing that pre-training enhances molecular structure awareness (especially in upper layers), and that fine-tuning predominantly alters task-relevant substructure representations, indicating that representation changes follow chemical theory.
